shots.composition_notes: Locked-off symmetrical two-shot of the couple in matching salon pedicure chairs, dead center-framed with equal headroom on both. A third character (the wife, glimpsed via mirror reflection) sits blurred in the left background, establishing the salon as a shared/public space. Bottom of frame cuts off at the foot-soak bowls; subtitle burned in at lower-center between the two chairs so it doesn't overlap either face.

Cut in tighter on the same static camera position/angle as scene 1 — no pan or dolly, just a harder lens/crop. Woman is placed left-of-center per rule-of-thirds and fully legible; the man's face is pushed hard against the right frame edge and partially cropped, turning him into a reactive foreground silhouette rather than a full subject. Background salon-chair woman still visible bottom-left for spatial continuity.

Hard cut to a dead-center close-up isolating the husband's face and glass of cucumber water, cropping the wife out of frame entirely for the punchline reaction. Symmetrical framing with generous headroom above his slicked hair, deep-focus salon row blurred behind him. His deadpan/unimpressed expression is the sole focal point.
Black title/credit card ('LOW BATTERY PEOPLE / Created by Nin.') centered on screen — no live-action camera framing, pure typographic end card.

framing_patterns_notes: The sequence tightens shot by shot rather than cutting between angles: wide symmetrical two-shot -> tighter two-shot crop (same static camera position) -> isolated close-up on the reacting character, a punch-in progression that ends on the deadpan face for the joke's payoff. Every live-action shot is completely static (no pans, tilts, or zooms detected across periodic frames within a scene) — comedic timing is carried entirely by cuts and dialogue, not camera motion. Compositions are consistently center-weighted and symmetrical, with characters' faces kept in the vertical middle of frame and subtitles placed low so they never cross a face.
